KO.rationale: Coca-Cola is a high-quality defensive franchise with excellent brand equity, a 64-year dividend increase streak, and an asset-light concentrate model that supports strong margins (62% gross, 28% operating, 26% net) and high ROE (~40%). The business is fundamentally healthy with solid Q2 2025 results (revenue $12.54B, EPS $0.88, +14% QoQ EPS growth) and positive news sentiment (mean 0.675 over 90 days). However, the stock is trading at the top of its 1-year P/E range (29.2x vs. 23.2-29.8x window), near all-time highs at $82.63, and offers only a ~3.4% earnings yield — not compelling for a mid-single-digit grower. The $20B IRS tax dispute is a material overhang, and rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.54%) compress the relative attractiveness of a 2.6% dividend yield. Q2 earnings on July 28 could be a modest catalyst, but consensus expects only 5.8% EPS growth, limiting re-rating potential. The stock is fairly to slightly richly valued for its growth profile, capping upside.
